findings.title: Missing `paths`/`paths-ignore` on Expensive Workflows
findings.evidence: workflow triggers on pull_request/push but declares no `paths:`/`paths-ignore:` filter (the `on:` block below has no `paths:` key). NOTE: if this workflow is a REQUIRED status check, add a per-job `dorny/paths-filter` gate that returns a neutral pass — a workflow-level `paths:` filter would strand the required check on excluded PRs.
findings.evidence_snippet:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    # The branches below must be a subset of the branches above
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 23 * * 0'
findings.size_note: below the cluster floor — runner-minute (bill) only, no wall-clock
findings.runner_min_note: gross upper bound — assumes every irrelevant run runs the full job and a `paths:` filter skips it; realizable only where the workflow's jobs don't ALREADY self-skip (via `if:` guards or an internal change-gate) and the trigger can be narrowed safely — verify per workflow before crediting

measured_evidence.summary: 7 run(s) across 1 branch(es) were superseded (a newer run started before they finished) in the sampled window; ~2–15 runner-min/mo of superseded compute (mean over 4 timed run(s); ×0.27 to the 30d volume (27 runs); 100-run recent slice (not a full 30d census)). Superseded attribution is INFERENCE — the API marks no run 'cancelled-by-concurrency'.
measured_evidence.note: Superseded = a run a NEWER run started before it finished — measured by timestamp overlap, so sequential (non-racing) commits are NOT charged. Cancellation cause is unknowable from the API, so the attribution is INFERENCE. Basis: the count is from the all-status slice (100 runs); the per-run PRICE is the mean of 4 PR-success timed runs (superseded runs' own jobs aren't fetched) — different populations. findings.title: Matrix Leg Imbalance
findings.evidence: leg `build (3.15-dev, windows-latest)` median 273s vs `build (3.11, ubuntu-22.04)` 95s — 2.9× imbalance over 161 sampled runs (heterogeneous legs — split the slow leg, don't rebalance)
findings.measured_signal: leg `build (3.15-dev, windows-latest)` median 273s vs `build (3.11, ubuntu-22.04)` 95s — 2.9× imbalance over 161 sampled runs (heterogeneous legs — split the slow leg, don't rebalance)
findings.size_note: split the slow leg `build (3.15-dev, windows-latest)`; saving (~1s) is bounded by the next-slowest leg (272s)

measured_evidence.summary: Across 161 sampled `build` runs, the slowest leg (`build (3.15-dev, windows-latest)`, median 273s) is 2.9× the fastest (`build (3.11, ubuntu-22.04)`, 95s) and gates the matrix. These legs do DIFFERENT work, so they cannot be rebalanced — the slow leg is the long pole.
measured_evidence.note: Each link opens that leg's worst observed run. Fix: SPLIT the slowest leg `build (3.15-dev, windows-latest)` itself (sub-shard its suite, or split its backends into parallel jobs) — not rebalance across legs. That floors at the next-slowest leg `build (3.14t, windows-latest)` (272s), which becomes the new pole, so the realistic first-step saving is ~1s; split that leg next to go lower.

findings.title: Repeated Workflow Attempts From Same Failing Job
findings.evidence: 4 sampled run_attempt>1 workflow run(s) had prior-attempt jobs present in `filter=all` but absent from `filter=latest`; the unique dominant failing job was `build (3.13, windows-latest)` (4 failed/timed-out prior-attempt job(s), 13.3 failed min) and it appeared again in the latest attempt. ~74 runner-min/mo of prior-attempt compute (29/30d ÷ 100 sampled all-status run(s)).
findings.measured_signal: run_attempt>1 prior-attempt job delta from filter=all minus filter=latest; dominant failing job `build (3.13, windows-latest)` present in latest attempt (256.9 sampled prior-attempt min; scale 0.29)
findings.size_note: runner-minute (bill) only — prior workflow attempts are superseded by the latest attempt's signal.

measured_evidence.summary: 4 sampled run_attempt>1 workflow run(s) had prior-attempt jobs present in `filter=all` but absent from `filter=latest`; the unique dominant failing job was `build (3.13, windows-latest)` (4 failed/timed-out prior-attempt job(s), 13.3 failed min) and it appeared again in the latest attempt. ~74 runner-min/mo of prior-attempt compute (29/30d ÷ 100 sampled all-status run(s)).
measured_evidence.note: Measured from GitHub jobs API `filter=all` minus `filter=latest` for workflow runs whose run_attempt > 1. The finding is emitted only when each credited prior attempt has the same unique dominant failed/timed-out job and that dominant failing job appears in the latest attempt; ambiguous ties, mixed-cause attempts, and retry-only volume are withheld.

tier2_neutrality.ref: run_attempt>1: `filter=all` exposes prior-attempt jobs, `filter=latest` is the superseding latest attempt; the dominant failing job `build (3.13, windows-latest)` identifies the retry cause, so prior-attempt compute is post-completion waste

findings.size_note: runner-minute (bill) only — superseded runs don't gate the merge (the latest run does); range is lower(overlap-confirmed)–upper(naive runs-1).

Superseded attribution is INFERENCE — the API marks no run 'cancelled-by-concurrency'.
measured_evidence.note: Superseded = a run a NEWER run started before it finished — measured by timestamp overlap, so sequential (non-racing) commits are NOT charged. Cancellation cause is unknowable from the API, so the attribution is INFERENCE. Basis: the count is from the all-status slice (100 runs); the per-run PRICE is the mean of 5 PR-success timed runs (superseded runs' own jobs aren't fetched) — different populations. GUARDRAIL: verify this is NOT a deploy/release/publish workflow (a mid-flight run may be uploading artifacts / pushing a tag) before enabling cancellation — and take the predicate from the catalog recipe, which scopes cancellation with an expression; never a bare `cancel-in-progress: true`, which also kills in-flight runs on the default branch and on release tags. ROUTING: this workflow triggers on `pull_request`/`push` — with a `pull_request` trigger use the catalog's DEFAULT (PR-scoped) predicate; without one, the PR-scoped predicate is never true and saves nothing, so use the catalog's WIDENED predicate.

findings.title: Shared step recurs across the cluster — fix once, lower the floor
findings.evidence: the `Run tests` step is 65% of the slowest cluster job `build (3.14t, windows-latest)` (269s) and recurs across 7 concurrent jobs of `.github/workflows/run-tests.yml` (~176–180s per job) — a cluster-floor lever
findings.measured_signal: the `Run tests` step is 65% of the slowest cluster job `build (3.14t, windows-latest)` (269s) and recurs across 7 concurrent jobs of `.github/workflows/run-tests.yml` (~176–180s per job) — a cluster-floor lever
findings.size_note: cluster-floor lever — saving credited across all 7 jobs running the shared `test` step (~562 runner-min/mo); wall-clock capped at the measured critical-path floor — `build (3.10, macOS-latest)` (160s) is a slower concurrent check on a representative PR
findings.guardrail: make each parallel copy cheap (shared warm cache / prebuilt base image) — do NOT consolidate into one upstream job the others needs: (that adds a serial gate, OPT14/wall-clock-negative); verify the cache key captures the step's real inputs so a hit never serves stale artifacts
findings.rollout: ship the shared cache, measure the cluster FLOOR (second-tallest job p50) before/after across 5 PRs — the win shows only when the whole cluster comes down
findings.failure_mode: low — caching a shared setup step changes no test/build semantics; escalates only if the shared step is a build whose cache could serve stale outputs

measured_evidence.summary: The **`Run tests`** (`test`) step is the root-cause cost in 7 concurrent critical-path jobs of `.github/workflows/run-tests.yml` — **65% of the slowest job** (`build (3.14t, windows-latest)`, 269s). The SAME step runs in each, so optimizing it once lowers all of them at the same time (shared floor ~176s, the cheapest job's cost).
measured_evidence.note: Cluster-floor lever: shaving any one pole stops at the floor, but the same step shared across concurrent jobs lowers all of them together. Credit spans every job that runs it.

wall_clock_derivation.reason: wall-clock capped at the measured critical-path floor — `build (3.10, macOS-latest)` (160s) is a slower concurrent check on a representative PR
